Alright, the latest test run showed that the two clients aren’t seeing each other: client A reports zero remote players while client B sees one. That asymmetry is clearly a multiplayer synchronization bug that I need to investigate directly. I already drafted a debugging script (saved to /tmp/dbg-mp.mjs) that spins up a server, launches two headless Chrome pages, connects both clients, and then runs a series of checks while printing any page errors. When I tried to execute it straight from /tmp, Node threw a module resolution error:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'puppeteer‑core' imported from /tmp/dbg-mp.mjs
```

That makes sense: Node resolves modules relative to the script’s directory, and /tmp doesn’t have a node_modules folder with the project’s dependencies. The repository’s test directory (`/home/lane/AIArchives/archives/neonstrike/test`) does have a proper `node_modules` hierarchy (including puppeteer‑core, puppeteer, etc.) because it’s part of the project. If I run the script from there, the import should succeed.

So the fix is simple: copy the temporary script into the test directory, then execute it there. I’ll also keep the script file around only for this run, so I’ll delete it afterwards to avoid clutter. There’s a tiny nuance with the server spawn command: it uses `cwd: '../app'` to start the server from the `app` folder, which is correct when the script lives in `test`. The original script already has that path, but just to be safe I’ll run a `sed` that does a no‑op replacement of `'../app'` with `'../app'`. This is effectively a placeholder in case I ever need to tweak the path, and it also forces `sed` to touch the file so the copy‑and‑run step is explicit.

Now I need to construct a Bash command that:
1. Copies `/tmp/dbg-mp.mjs` into the current working directory (which is the `test` folder, because that’s where I’m issuing the command from).
2. Runs `sed -i` to perform the harmless replacement.
3. Executes the script with `node dbg-mp.mjs`.
4. Cleans up by removing the copied script.

I’ll chain these with `&&` so that each step only proceeds if the previous one succeeded. I’ll also set a reasonable timeout (120 seconds) because the script launches a server and two browsers and may take a bit of time, but it shouldn’t run indefinitely.

Thus the final command will be:

```
cp /tmp/dbg-mp.mjs ./dbg-mp.mjs && sed -i "s#'../app'#'../app'#" dbg-mp.mjs && node dbg-mp.mjs; rm -f dbg-mp.mjs
```

I’ll wrap this in a Bash tool call with a description that makes clear I’m running the multiplayer debug from the test directory with the proper dependencies. This should resolve the module‑not‑found error and let me see the detailed logs that will help pinpoint why client A isn’t receiving the remote player data.

arguments.command: cp /tmp/dbg-mp.mjs ./dbg-mp.mjs && sed -i "s#'../app'#'../app'#" dbg-mp.mjs && node dbg-mp.mjs; rm -f dbg-mp.mjs
arguments.description: Run multiplayer debug from test dir with deps
